nodes.title: Admissible geometric coefficient towers
nodes.statement: Let G act continuously on a site S and W be a finite flat local domain over Z_p, W_l=W/p^l. A bounded-below equivariant derived W_l-tower C is admissible if every H^q(S,C_l) is a discrete continuous G-module and R¹lim_l H^q(S,C_l) is killed by a power of p, for every q. Put C_L=(Rlim_l C_l)⊗_W L for a finite product L of finite extensions of Frac(W), hence flat over W. Its geometric cohomology is canonically (lim_l H^q(S,C_l))⊗_W L, with the inverse-limit topology followed by rationalization; the displayed isomorphism is part of the interface, not a discrete topology on its right side.
hypotheses: The derived inverse limit is taken before inverting p; the finite-exponent bound may depend on q.
G-equivariant sheaves and their continuous derived global sections are imported from the arithmetic-duality supplier.
proofSteps: Use the supplier Milnor sequence to identify the possible obstruction as R¹lim H^{q−1}.
Flatness of L over W lets cohomology and the Milnor sequence commute with tensoring; the p-power torsion obstruction then disappears. Retain the inverse-limit topology for the cochain comparison.

nodes.title: Geometric Hochschild–Serre edge map
nodes.statement: For an admissible tower C there is a functorial first-quadrant, degreewise convergent spectral sequence H^a_cont(G,H^b(S,C_L)) ⇒ H^{a+b}_G(S,C_L), with the usual shift if C is only bounded below. Define H^q_G(S,C_L)_0 as the kernel of the geometric forgetful map to H^q(S,C_L). The filtration edge gives ε_C:H^q_G(S,C_L)_0→H¹_cont(G,H^{q−1}(S,C_L)). Its image lies in E₂^{1,q−1}; ε is not asserted injective on the whole kernel.
hypotheses: C is admissible as defined above; cohomology is continuous for the limit topology.

For the stated finite flat local domain W and Frac(W)-algebra L, restrict scalars to Z_p for the continuous comparison and use flat extension to L; an arbitrary map from a finite flat Z_p-algebra to a field is insufficient.
proofSteps: Apply the D7 Grothendieck spectral sequence to geometric sections followed by G-invariants on discrete finite-level equivariant sheaves.
Use acyclic equivariant resolutions and the requested continuous inverse-limit comparison, rather than the group-quotient spectral sequence alone.
The vanishing in filtration degree zero identifies the kernel with filtration F¹; project F¹→F¹/F²=E∞^{1,q−1} and include this subspace in E₂^{1,q−1}.

sources.match: Constructs the geometric site spectral sequence and its first edge on the geometric kernel.

acceptance: For C concentrated geometrically in degree zero, the degree-one edge is the usual continuous H¹ identification.

nodes.title: Connecting cocycles with fixed signs
nodes.statement: In a distinguished triangle A→B→C→A[1] of admissible objects, represent the triangle by compatible cochain complexes with differentials of degree +1. Let b∈Z^q(B)^G and choose c∈C^{q−1} with dc=νb and a=b−dy∈Z^q(A), where y lifts c to B. Then the projected edge of ν[b] is represented by g↦gc−c in H^{q−1}(C)/im H^{q−1}(B). Under the connecting map δ([z])=[d(lift z)] its value is [a−ga]. Equivalently it is ga−a after choosing the connecting map −δ. State the sign whenever this description is used.
hypotheses: The image of ν[b] in geometric H^q(C) is zero.
An equivariant acyclic resolution gives a representative b that is G-fixed; replace the original complexes by that resolution if necessary.
Replace the triangle by a degreewise split short exact sequence of cochain complexes before choosing y; compatible derived maps alone do not specify a cochain lift.
proofSteps: Choose y and compute a=b−dy, then d(gy−y)=a−ga.
Changing y or c changes the displayed cochain by the appropriate coboundary or the image from H^{q−1}(B).
Pass through the geometric edge and the quotient; use −δ in the shifted −N monodromy triangle consistently.

sources.match: Extracts the triangle calculation with an explicit cohomological convention, avoiding reliance on the typographical slips in the printed representatives.

acceptance: A two-term complex with a nontrivial connecting map detects reversal of δ; both normalized formulas must give the same kernel comparison.
The formula descends through im H^{q−1}(B).

nodes.title: Finite étale correspondences and support transport
nodes.statement: For a scheme X take isomorphism classes of spans X←f X₁→g X with both legs finite étale, composed by fiber product. EC(X) is their unital integral monoid algebra. A ring T of correspondences is a commutative L-algebra with a unital L-algebra homomorphism into EC(X)⊗L. For a basis span set S_t=f(g⁻¹S), t∨=(g,f), and t*=f_*g* on cycles and cohomology. For a finite formal sum, define S_t by the union over its nonzero coefficients. If 𝒰⊆𝒳 is open, set 𝒰_t=𝒳∖(𝒳∖𝒰)_{t∨}; then t* transports proper-support cohomology from U_t to U. Cancellation can make this support bound strict.
hypotheses: L is a finite product of p-adic fields.
The commutative T convention is used for maximal ideals and localizations in HP.4–HP.5; noncommutative localization is outside this target.
proofSteps: Use finite étale base change and trace to define span composition and its action.
Extend linearly from the monoid algebra; do not impose a Chow-equivalence quotient on EC(X).
The transpose support condition ensures that a section supported properly in U_t pushes to one supported properly in U.

nodes.title: Geometrically trivial cycles and Selmer-restricted cycles
nodes.statement: For X/K proper smooth of pure dimension n−1, let Z^d(X)^0_L be the kernel of the geometric class map Z^d(X)⊗L→H^{2d}(X_Kbar,L(d)). The geometric edge applied to the arithmetic cycle class defines AJ_X(c)∈H¹(K,H^{2d−1}(X_Kbar,L(d))). For V⊆H^{2d−1}(X_Kbar,L(d)), put Z^d_V(X)^0_L={c:AJ_X(c) lies in im H¹(K,V)}. A lift to H¹(K,V) is canonical only when H⁰(K,H/V)=0; HP.1 verifies that hypothesis in its geometric situation.
hypotheses: Arithmetic cycle classes and refined classes are the EDC.3 objects.
The geometric triviality condition is weaker than vanishing of the arithmetic class.
proofSteps: Take the kernel of the EDC.3 geometric cycle map, with its L-module structure.
Apply the geometric edge to the arithmetic cycle class and use naturality.
Define the V-restricted domain by inverse image; uniqueness follows from the Galois-cohomology exact sequence once H⁰(H/V)=0 is supplied.

nodes.title: Mixed extension of disjoint cycles
nodes.statement: Let c∈Z^d(X)^0_L and c′∈Z^{d′}(X)^0_L, d+d′=n, with disjoint supports. For disjoint pure-codimension supports Z,Z′ choose κ_c:L→H_Z^{2d}(X_Kbar,L(d)) and κ_c′:H^{2d−2}(Z′_Kbar,L(d−1))→L, the refined cycle map and the trace pairing with c′. Pull back and push out the localization diagram along κ_c and κ_c′(1). This produces a mixed extension E(c,c′) with rows 0→L(1)→E_c′→H→0 and 0→L(1)→E(c,c′)→E_c→0 and columns 0→H→E_c→L→0 and 0→E_c′→E(c,c′)→L→0, where H=H^{2d−1}(X_Kbar,L(d)). It is independent up to canonical compatible isomorphism of the enlarged supports. Its three classes are AJ(c), AJ(c′) in H¹(K,H∨(1)), and e(c,c′)∈H¹(K,E_c′).
hypotheses: 1≤d,d′≤n−1; zero cycles are handled by split extensions without requiring nonempty supports.
Poincaré duality identifies H∨(1) with H^{2d′−1}(X_Kbar,L(d′)).
The construction uses proper smooth X, as in A.7; A.3 states its projective case. Enhanced localization and Poincaré duality provide the same diagram without projectivity.
proofSteps: Use EDC localization, purity and Poincaré duality to obtain the four exact sequences in the A.2 diagram.
Geometric triviality makes κ_c land in the localization kernel and makes κ_c′ vanish on the image from X with twist d−1.
Pull back on the L endpoint and push out on the L(1) endpoint. Compare support enlargements through their union to obtain independence.
Compare the resulting connecting classes with the geometric edge using the fixed cochain signs.

nodes.title: Local index away from p
nodes.statement: Let K be nonarchimedean of residue characteristic ℓ≠p. For disjoint cycles as in HP.0 assume AJ(c)=AJ(c′)=0 locally. Then both marginal extension classes vanish and e(c,c′) has a unique preimage in H¹(K,L(1)) under H¹(K,L(1))→H¹(K,E_c′). Define the local Kummer index by this preimage, using H¹(K,L(1))≃(lim_m K×/(K×)^{p^m})⊗_{Z_p}L. If, in addition, both arithmetic cycle classes vanish in H^{2d}(X,L(d)) and H^{2d′}(X,L(d′)), one can also lift the refined classes to γ∈H^{2d−1}(X∖Z,L(d)) and γ′∈H^{2d′−1}(X∖Z′,L(d′)), then apply Mayer–Vietoris boundary and trace to γ∪γ′. This second realization is the Beilinson index on that stronger domain.
hypotheses: The residue characteristic is different from p.

Vanishing of both marginal AJ classes suffices for the Kummer preimage. The cup-product comparison additionally requires both arithmetic cycle classes to vanish; geometric triviality alone supplies neither hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use the two zero marginal classes and the exact cohomology sequence of 0→L(1)→E_c′→H→0 to get existence and injectivity of the preimage.
Use the parent Kummer identification with the multiplicative completion, retaining the completion before tensoring.
Localization gives γ and γ′, and Mayer–Vietoris and trace give the second description; independence is established by the next comparison.

proofSteps: Represent the two localization sequences by a compatible mapping-cone diagram and the two refined classes by cocycles.

nodes.title: The Panchishkin subrepresentation
nodes.statement: For a de Rham finite-dimensional L-representation V of G_K, K/Q_p finite, a Panchishkin subrepresentation is a G_K-stable subspace V⁺ such that Fil⁰D_dR(V⁺)=0 and Fil⁰D_dR(V/V⁺)=D_dR(V/V⁺). Existence is a property; when it holds V⁺ is unique. Write V⁻=V/V⁺. The induced splitting of D_dR(V)→D_dR(V)/Fil⁰ is the one with image D_dR(V⁺). No vanishing of H⁰(K,V⁻) is included in this definition.
hypotheses: The category is the imported de Rham representation category, and filtrations use the convention D_dR(Q_p(1)) has Fil⁰=0.
proofSteps: Express the two filtration conditions on the existing de Rham realization.

For two candidates, the image of V⁺→V/W⁺ is a de Rham subquotient. Strict exactness makes its Fil⁰ zero from the source and everything from the target; it is zero. Apply in both directions. This uses exactness and faithfulness of D_dR, not fullness of D_dR on arbitrary filtered maps.
Strictness gives the direct-sum decomposition D_dR(V)=D_dR(V⁺)⊕Fil⁰D_dR(V).

nodes.title: Crystalline Panchishkin criterion and extension stability
nodes.statement: For crystalline V let D⁺⊆D_cris(V) be its strictly negative Newton-slope subspace, with the induced Hodge filtration after extension to K. V is Panchishkin if and only if D⁺ is weakly admissible and D⁺⊗_{K₀}K is a complement to Fil⁰D_dR(V). In that case D⁺=D_cris(V⁺). In an exact sequence 0→V₁→V→V₂→0 in which all three representations are crystalline, a common nonzero integer purity weight of V₁,V₂ passes to V, and the Panchishkin property of V₁,V₂ passes to V.
hypotheses: Weak admissibility includes all filtered φ-subobject inequalities, not just equality of total Hodge and Newton degrees.
The extension assertion is inside the crystalline category; it does not assert that every extension of crystalline representations is crystalline.
proofSteps: For V⁺, Fil⁰=0 forces every Newton slope negative by weak admissibility; the quotient has only nonnegative slopes.
Conversely apply weak-admissibility-is-admissibility to D⁺ and strictness to identify its quotient, then recover V⁺.

nodes.title: Finite Abel–Jacobi classes for pure semistable summands
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, X/K smooth proper, H=H^{2d−1}(X_Kbar,L(d)), and V⊆H a G_K-subrepresentation. Assume H^i(K_v,V)=0 for every i and every finite v∤p, and that V|G_{K_v} is semistable pure of weight −1 for v|p. Then every c∈Z^d_V(X)^0_L has a unique AJ lift in H¹_f(K,V). Here H⁰(K,H/V)=0 is supplied by a good-reduction Frobenius with weight −1 on H/V, not by a claim that all quotients of a monodromy-pure local representation are pure of weight −1.

Purity at p is monodromy/Weil–Deligne purity.

Realize AJ as an extension subquotient of the cohomology of the open complement of its support; request the smooth-open potential semistability theorem, including localization and pullback compatibility.
A potentially semistable extension of the semistable V by L is semistable: finite inertial type in its associated potentially semistable module is unipotent and hence trivial in characteristic zero.

nodes.title: Canonical local height of finite mixed extensions
nodes.statement: For K/Q_p finite, V semistable pure of weight −1 with its Panchishkin subrepresentation, and V′ paired G_K-equivariantly with V into L(1), consider mixed extensions with marginal classes in H¹_f(K,V) and H¹_f(K,V′). The Hodge splitting D_dR(V⁺)⊕Fil⁰ defines Nekovář’s canonical local splitting of the associated Kummer torsor. Write h_K(e) for its value in (lim_m K×/(K×)^{p^m})⊗L, normalized compatibly with the non-p local index. Translation of the mixed extension by a∈H¹(K,L(1)) translates h_K by a. For the cycle mixed extensions in this setting, e∈H¹_f(K,E_c′) if and only if h_K(e) belongs to the image of completed O_K×⊗L. The construction includes the exceptional-quotient terms when H⁰(K,V⁻)≠0.

A pairing V×V′→L(1) may be degenerate; reduce by pullback from the dual representation rather than assume it perfect.

nodes.title: Global height and its cycle decomposition
nodes.statement: For a number field K let Γ_{K,p} be the p-completion of the finite idele group A_K^{∞,×} modulo K× and the local unit groups away from p; retain its torsion until tensoring with L. For V,V′ satisfying the two local hypotheses of abel-jacobi-finite-condition and the Panchishkin condition at every v|p, a G_K-pairing V×V′→L(1) gives an L-bilinear canonical height H¹_f(K,V)×H¹_f(K,V′)→Γ_{K,p}⊗_{Z_p}L. Pull it back along the unique finite AJ lifts to obtain the cycle height on Z^d_V(X)^0_L×Z^{d′}_{V′}(X)^0_L. For disjoint representatives it is the sum over finite places of their local mixed-extension indices: first map each local completed K_v×⊗L into Γ_{K,p}⊗L by the idelic map, then add. Away from p use the Kummer/Nekovář index: (V1) makes both marginal AJ classes zero. It equals the Beilinson index under the additional arithmetic-vanishing hypotheses of that comparison. At p use the canonical local height.
hypotheses: V and V′ satisfy (V1) local acyclicity away from p, (V2) semistability and purity −1 at p, and (V3) Panchishkin at p.
For cycles require X smooth proper of dimension n−1, d+d′=n, the chosen embeddings of V and V′ in the complementary cohomology groups, and the induced Poincaré pairing.
proofSteps: Use the parent global duality and orthogonality to choose a global lift of one finite extension through the other dual extension.

Apply the canonical local splittings; (V1) kills both non-p marginal AJ classes and hence gives the unique Kummer preimage. Use the Beilinson comparison only when its stronger arithmetic-vanishing hypotheses hold. Almost all scalar local terms vanish by integral extension and unramifiedness.
The difference of two global lifts is a global Kummer class, whose sum in Γ vanishes by global reciprocity. This proves choice independence.

nodes.title: Supported syntomic Abel–Jacobi domain
nodes.statement: Let 𝒳/O_K be proper strictly semistable of relative dimension n−1, X its special fiber, 𝒰⊆𝒳 open with generic fiber U, and F:U_s→X. Import Kato’s integral log-syntomic tower S(d)_𝒳 and Sato’s twists, for 0≤d<p−1. Define Syn_c(𝒰,d)=RΓ(X_et,F!F*S(d)_𝒳,Q_p). Its comparison map π goes to RΓ_c(U,Q_p(d)). Define H^q(Syn_c)^♥=π⁻¹(ker(H^q_c(U,Q_p(d))→H^q_c(U_Kbar,Q_p(d)))). The map α_q is the geometric edge after π followed by Q_p(d)→B_cris, with target H¹(K,H^{q−1}_c(U_Kbar,Q_p)⊗B_cris). The heart is an inverse image under π, not the kernel of forgetting G on the syntomic complex.

nodes.title: The log-rigid obstruction map
nodes.statement: Use the imported supported log-convergent complexes ω_(U_s,X) and ω̃_(U_s,X) and their monodromy triangle. The syntomic-to-crystalline map followed by specialization gives ξ:Syn_c(𝒰,d)→RΓ(X_et,ω̃_(U_s,X)). Call 𝒰 d-dense when dim(X^{(h)}∖U_s^{(h)})≤d−h for every h≥1, using RD.4’s predicate. If d≥1 and 𝒰 is d-dense, the composite from H^{2d}(Syn_c)^♥ to H^{2d}_rig((U_s,X)/W°) is zero. The triangle therefore gives a unique map ρ_{2d}:H^{2d}(Syn_c)^♥→H^{2d−1}_rig((U_s,X)/W°)/N; its composite with the triangle’s injective boundary equals H^{2d}(ξ). The quotient by the image of N is essential.

nodes.statement: Let c∈Z^d(X_K)^0_L have closure contained in a d-dense 𝒰. The Sato refined cycle class in T(d)_𝒳 maps through T(d)_𝒳→S(d)_𝒳 to σ_c∈H^{2d}(Syn_c(𝒰,d)_L)^♥. Therefore ρ_{2d}(σ_c) lies in the kernel of H^{2d−1}_rig((U_s,X)/W°)_L/N→H^{2d−1}(X_et,ω⁺_(U_s,X))_L.

The residue of the refined cycle in logarithmic Hodge–Witt cohomology is zero by the requested Sato Prop. 9.10 interface. This supplies the supported syntomic lift and its zero positive residue.
The complement dimension bound gives H^{2d−1}(X_Kbar∖U_Kbar,L(d))=0 and thus injectivity H_c^{2d}(U_Kbar,L(d))→H^{2d}(X_Kbar,L(d)). Geometric triviality therefore puts σ_c in the supported heart.

Put 𝒱=𝒳′∖𝒰′ and let 𝒱(h) be the disjoint union of h-fold intersections of its components, 𝒱(0)=𝒳′. For each coefficient complex, define the supported object indexed by h=−1 as Tot(C⁰→C¹→⋯), placing Cʰ in horizontal degree h, with its augmentation to C⁰; for one boundary this is Cone(C⁰→C¹)[−1]. The label h=−1 introduces no additional cohomological shift. nodes.title: The supported period diagram of an altered pair
nodes.statement: On the boundary strata of a chosen altered pair take compatible Galois-equivariant log-PD embedding systems over W[t]°. At each finite p-power level and each finite Galois coefficient extension use the PD de Rham complex with degree-j term J^[r−j]⊗Ω^j over W with trivial base log structure (J^[a]=O for a≤0), with its divided Frobenius. Taking the coefficient-extension colimit gives barred B(r); B(0) is barred C_triv. Replacing relative differentials by those over W[t]° gives barred C_log. Set barred S(r)=fib(incl−φ_r:B(r)→C_triv), where φ_r denotes the degree-compatible integral map p^(−r)φ supplied by the Kato divided-Frobenius construction. Take the boundary totalization for h=−1 and push from the embedding hypercover to X_et. The unbarred objects use the initial coefficient extension without that colimit. The diagram includes ξ_r:S(r)→C_triv, π_r:S(r)→near-cycles(r), the log monodromy triangle C_log[−1]→C_triv→C_log→^N C_log, and specialization to the W° complexes.

Compares both realizations before taking the edge map.

nodes.title: Admissibility and cohomology of the boundary period diagram
nodes.statement: For every boundary index h≥−1 and degree q, the specialized unbarred C_W° realizes H^q_rig(V(h)/W°), compatibly with N. The unbarred C_log, barred C_log and barred C_triv are admissible towers. If D_q=H^q_rig(V(h)/W°), their cohomology is respectively D_q⊗_{K₀}𝒦, D_q⊗_{K₀}B̂_st⁺ and (D_q⊗_{K₀}B_st⁺)^{N=0}, with the diagonal monodromy on the last two tensors. Here 𝒦 and B̂_st⁺ are the PH R06.1 period rings, with their given limit topology. The assertions include the supported index h=−1. No assertion of admissibility of unbarred C_triv is made.
hypotheses: Use the compatible Galois embedding and PD systems of boundary-period-diagram.
Tensor statements are rational and have the canonical continuous G_K,φ,N compatibilities.
proofSteps: For proper strata use the requested p^a-almost crystalline comparison and finite-coefficient finiteness to bound R¹lim; rationalization kills the bounded torsion.
The boundary alternating complex is exact on supported tube sections, giving the h=−1 log-rigid identification, not just an unspecified dimension equality.
Transport the finite proper-stratum comparisons through the bounded totalization and its long exact sequences. Flatness of the relevant period scalar extensions gives the cohomology base changes.
Use the monodromy exact sequence and PH’s completed-period nilpotent part to identify barred C_triv with the N-invariants of D_q⊗B_st⁺.

sources.match: Supplies exactly the admissible objects and their base-change identities needed for the continuous edge calculation.

acceptance: Verify the supported h=−1 case by the boundary resolution.
Check that N on D_q⊗B_st⁺ is the diagonal operator, so N-invariants are not replaced by D_q^{N=0}⊗B_cris⁺.

nodes.title: Period comparison with compatible syntomic maps
nodes.statement: Assume n<p. For every boundary index h≥−1 there is a G_K,φ,N-compatible B_st comparison between its rational étale cohomology tensored with B_st and D_q⊗_{K₀}B_st. For n−1≤r<p−1 the boundary period map π_r is an equivalence; its composite with ξ_r produces this comparison and it is independent of the chosen such r. For 0≤d<p−1, the maps ξ_d and π_d fit the comparison square using Q_p(d)→B_cris⊆B_st. Moreover, the original supported syntomic map factors through S(d)_{V(−1)} on the chosen strict pair, compatibly with both π_d and ξ_d.
hypotheses: This is a supported strict-pair comparison built from proper-stratum comparison and coherent boundary maps.
The general open geometric comparison used in HP.1 is a separate supplier request, not inferred from an arbitrary proper theorem without supports.
proofSteps: Use the Kato/Tsuji stable-range period map on each stratum, with r≥n−1, and totalize the actual compatible diagram.
Use proper semistable comparison on each stratum and boundary compatibility to obtain the supported B_st comparison.
Compare different weights by syntomic cup product with the base-point Tate class; include filtration compatibility through the supplied period maps.
Extend the supported map through the boundary resolution using the strict pair’s log structures; verify both ξ and π composites.

sources.match: Identifies the compatible period morphisms needed for the edge comparison, not just an abstract vector-space isomorphism.

acceptance: Use r=n−1; n
The comparison must commute with both syntomic maps and boundary restriction, not merely identify dimensions.

nodes.title: Compatibility of the syntomic Abel–Jacobi edge
nodes.statement: For 0≤d<p−1, all h≥−1 and all q, the edge of a syntomic class whose étale image is geometrically zero is compatible with the map to H¹(K,(D_{q−1}⊗B_st⁺)^{N=0}), and then with the B_cris-valued étale edge under supported-period-comparison. This statement holds on the entire inverse-image heart, even when the class is not in the geometric kernel of syntomic cohomology itself.
hypotheses: n<p, and the period diagram and its coefficient maps use the fixed log/Frobenius conventions.
proofSteps: Choose n−1≤r<p−1 with r≥d. Cup with the base-point syntomic Tate class of weight r−d and retain the compensating Tate twist d−r.
The high-weight π_r is an equivalence; use it to lift the near-cycle map to a compatible derived diagram before applying equivariant sections.
Take the continuous edge of that derived diagram and then identify its period coefficient maps by period-cohomology.
This weight-raising argument is necessary because ordinary edge naturality alone does not apply to the larger syntomic heart.

sources.match: Provides the additional derived compatibility required by the heart definition.

acceptance: A proof that assumes every heart class is geometrically trivial syntomically does not pass.
The Tate twists r−d and d−r must cancel in the coefficient diagram.

nodes.title: Strict-pair kernel comparison in every degree
nodes.statement: On the chosen strict semistable pair with n
hypotheses: No density assumption is imposed on the altered open.
The monodromy connecting-map comparison is used only on the φ=p^{d−1} eigenspace of the completed log realization.
proofSteps: Use the injective period base change and ξ/π square to show vanishing of the heart in rigid cohomology in every degree (B.16).
Identify the geometric kernel of barred C_triv with the monodromy quotient of barred C_log using period-cohomology.
Apply triangle-edge-cocycle to the shifted monodromy triangle, whose first arrow is −N[−1]. The boundary shifts Frobenius eigenvalue p^{d−1} to p^d.
Use PH R06.1’s Frobenius-restricted monodromy-edge theorem and specialization 𝒦→K₀ to get equality of the two kernels in (B.39). Do not extend that result to the full monodromy quotient.
Use syntomic-edge-compatibility to conclude the inclusion for α′_q.

sources.match: Proves the strict-pair kernel statement with the Frobenius restriction and monodromy sign retained.

acceptance: The proof cannot assume the altered open is d-dense.
Diagram B.40 is checked on φ=p^{d−1}; the statement does not assert that δ factors through specialization on the entire space.

nodes.title: Kernel comparison after one finite extension
nodes.statement: Let n<p, 1≤d<p−1 and 𝒰 be d-dense in the original proper strictly semistable 𝒳. There exists a finite K_𝒰/K depending on 𝒰 but not on the syntomic class such that ker ρ_{2d}⊆ker(res_{K_𝒰}∘α_{2d}). For 𝒰=𝒳 one may take K_𝒰=K. The conclusion is a kernel comparison after restriction, not a claim that potentially crystalline extension classes always descend as crystalline.
hypotheses: Use the source/target of ρ and α from HP.2 with their proper support and Tate twists.
proofSteps: Choose the altered pair once, with coefficient extension K′. Its open need not be dense; strict-pair-kernel-comparison nevertheless applies in every degree.
Pull back the original syntomic class and obstruction through the compatible support map. If its original ρ vanishes, so does the altered one.

The proper generically finite map on generic opens has compact-support pullback with a G_K′-equivariant trace splitting after division by its degree, by Poincaré duality. This remains split after tensoring B_cris, so the induced H¹ map is injective.
Descend the zero edge from the altered representation to the original one over K′. In the proper case use the original strict semistable model directly.

sources.match: Transfers the strict-pair calculation back by a trace splitting, retaining the necessary finite extension.

acceptance: K_𝒰 is chosen from the altered pair once for all input classes.
The proper-open case takes K_𝒳=K; general finite-extension descent of crystallinity is not used.

nodes.title: Annihilation from a finite filtration
nodes.statement: Let T be a commutative ring, M a T-module, and 0=F₀⊆F₁⊆⋯⊆F_m=M a finite filtration. If an ideal I acts by zero on every F_{j+1}/F_j, then I^m M=0. Equivalently, a composite of m operators each lowering one filtration step is zero, also for a sequence of filtered modules and compatible lowering maps. As a signature available at the pins: for an R-linear endomorphism f of M with f(F_{j+1})⊆F_j, F₀=0 and F_m=M, one has f^m=0.
hypotheses: The filtration is exhaustive and starts at zero; it need not be strictly increasing.
For the multi-module version each factor lowers the filtration between its actual source and target.
proofSteps: An element of I sends F_{j+1} into F_j because it kills the corresponding quotient.
Induct on the number of factors: a product of r ideal elements sends F_j into F_{max(j−r,0)}.
After m factors the image is zero; extend from products to their additive span I^m.

sources.match: Isolates the algebraic proof milestone used by the geometric annihilator, with an actual native-carrier signature in the suggested file.

acceptance: For m=0 the hypotheses force M=0.
The Jordan block of size two is nonzero with square zero: replacing I^m by I is false.
A filtration of length m+1 needs m+1 lowering steps in general.

nodes.title: Deeper-stratum annihilation of the rigid obstruction
nodes.statement: Let 𝒳 be proper strictly semistable of relative dimension n−1, 1≤d≤n−1, and T its commutative L-correspondence algebra. Put D_deep=⊕_{h>1,q≥0}H^q_rig(X^{(h)}/K₀)⊗_{Q_p}L and I=Ann_T(D_deep). If 𝒰 is d-dense, then for every t∈I^{4n−5}, t* annihilates the kernel of H^{2d−1}_rig((U_{t,s},X)/W°)_L/N→H^{2d−1}(X_et,ω⁺_(U_{t,s},X))_L, with target support changed to U_s. The filtration induced from the supported weight spectral sequence has at most 4d−1 pieces, indexed 0 through 4d−2; its pieces on this kernel are subquotients of deeper-stratum cohomology.
hypotheses: The source is the support open 𝒰_t defined by the transpose correspondence; the target after t* uses 𝒰.
The positive complex ω⁺ is CR.6’s Sato residue variant; the weight and density comparisons are RD.4 imports.
proofSteps: Use RD.4’s supported weight spectral sequence and its projection onto the positive-support sequence.
The density comparison makes all non-deeper contributions to the indicated kernel vanish. Intersect the weight filtration with the monodromy quotient kernel.
Every remaining graded piece is a subquotient of D_deep, so each factor of I lowers its filtration. Use naturality with the actual sequence of support opens when composing factors.
Apply finite-filtration-annihilation. Since 4d−1≤4n−5, every element of I^{4n−5}, an additive sum of such products, kills the kernel.

sources.locator: Lemma B.10, pp. 343–344; Lemmas B.5–B.6, pp. 337–340
sources.match: Identifies the deeper-stratum filtration and the precise uniform annihilator exponent.

acceptance: Count 4d−1 pieces, not 4d−2. For d=n−1 the required bound is exactly 4n−5.
Do not treat t* as an endomorphism of supported cohomology on U_t; record its map to U.

nodes.title: Finite supported Abel–Jacobi classes after annihilation
nodes.statement: Under n<p, 1≤d≤n−1 and d-density of 𝒰, let t∈I^{4n−5} and let c∈Z^d(X_K)^0_L have closure in 𝒰_t. The arithmetic supported class has edge β_c∈H¹(K,H^{2d−1}_c(U_{t,Kbar},L(d))). Then res_{K_𝒰}(t*β_c)∈H¹_f(K_𝒰,H^{2d−1}_c(U_Kbar,L(d))). The extension K_𝒰 is chosen independently of c and t by the kernel-comparison theorem; for 𝒰=𝒳 it is K.
hypotheses: I is the deeper-stratum annihilator and t* has source support U_t and target support U.
The Bloch–Kato finite condition on arbitrary finite-dimensional cohomology is the kernel of the B_cris coefficient map.
proofSteps: Use the supported-cycle-lift σ_c with zero positive residue.
The deeper-stratum annihilator kills ρ(t*σ_c) by naturality and the stated filtration theorem.
Apply alteration-kernel-descent to conclude that the restricted B_cris-valued edge of t*σ_c vanishes.
By the definition of the finite condition and compatibility of π with the arithmetic cycle class, the restricted t*β_c is finite.

sources.locator: Proposition B.11 and its proof, pp. 344–346
sources.match: Converts the supported cycle lift and kernel comparison into the finite condition with the correct target open.

acceptance: The target is H_c(U), not H_c(U_t), after the correspondence acts.
The extension is not chosen separately for each cycle.

nodes.title: Crystalline pure localized cohomology
nodes.statement: Let m be a maximal ideal of the commutative correspondence algebra T such that (D_deep)_m=0. Then for every r the localized summand H^{2r−1}(X_Kbar,L(r))_m is crystalline and pure of weight −1. It is the idempotent summand cut out in the finite-dimensional image of T; no finite-dimensionality of T itself is required. The annihilator I has an element outside m, and I^a has one outside m for each a≥1.
hypotheses: The ambient scheme has a proper strictly semistable model, and all correspondence actions commute with φ,N.
Use all deeper-stratum degrees, rather than only the degree of the desired representation.
The proper weight sequence must carry the Frobenius, Tate twists and monodromy filtration specified in the RD.4 request; the existing underlying-vector-space statement does not supply them.
proofSteps: Use the requested Frobenius/monodromy refinement of RD.4’s proper weight sequence and the T-equivariant proper semistable comparison. After localization all h>1 terms vanish, so only the untwisted h=1 column remains; its cohomology in degree 2r−1 is smooth proper and monodromy is zero.

The requested N-filtration compatibility gives N=0 on the abutment, not just on a vector-space E₁ page. RD.6 purity and RD.7 Frobenius compatibility then give weight (2r−1)−2r=−1 after twist r, and proper semistable comparison identifies this N=0 summand as crystalline.
The image of T in the finite sum of the relevant cohomology groups is a finite-dimensional commutative Artinian L-algebra. Its primary idempotents split the localized summands.
Finite generation of D_deep and its zero localization gives I∖m nonempty; take powers for I^a.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem A.8, pp. 346–347; hypothesis (A.3), p. 327
sources.match: Produces the crystalline pure summand and the uniform correspondence choices needed for the full extension.

acceptance: For a smooth model the deeper-stratum module is zero and I=T.
Semistability without localized deeper-stratum vanishing is insufficient to conclude N=0.

nodes.title: Finite-condition exactness for the localized extension
nodes.statement: Put H=H^{2d−1}(X_Kbar,L(d)) and H′=H∨(1). Suppose the m′-localized summand H′_{m′} is crystalline pure of weight −1 and a short exact sequence 0→L(1)→E→H→0 has dual class in H¹_f(K,H′)∩H¹(K,H′_{m′}). For every finite K†/K the sequence 0→H¹_f(K†,L(1))→H¹_f(K†,E)→H¹_f(K†,H)→0 is exact. If H¹_♯(K†,E) is the inverse image of H¹_f(K†,H) in H¹(K†,E), the inclusion of this finite exact sequence into 0→H¹(K†,L(1))→H¹_♯(K†,E)→H¹_f(K†,H)→0 is a pushout.
hypotheses: H is proper semistable cohomology, but purity or crystallinity of its entire unlocalized representation is not assumed.
The extension is supported in the specified crystalline dual summand.
proofSteps: Split H and its dual by the finite-image idempotent. The extension is split on the complementary summand, where the finite-condition sequence is tautologically split.
On the selected summand use the crystalline finite-extension complex, strictness of D_dR and the absence of Frobenius eigenvalues 1 and p⁻¹ in weight −1.
This special exactness interface is a precise PH R06.2 request, replacing an unverified invocation of Nekovář 1993 Proposition 1.25 in broader generality.
Compare the two short exact sequences with the same right endpoint; their quotient is H¹(K†,L(1))/H¹_f(K†,L(1)), giving the pushout.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem A.8, property (*), (B.21), pp. 346–347, invoking Nekovář 1993 Proposition 1.25
sources.match: States the exact finite-condition input and its pushout on the correct localized summand.

acceptance: The exactness assertion is uniform in finite K†/K.
A proof assuming all of H crystalline or all short exact sequences preserve H¹_f misses the stated hypothesis.

nodes.title: Uniform crystalline cycle bi-extensions
nodes.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite, X/K smooth projective of dimension n−1, 𝒳/O_K a proper strictly semistable model, n<p, and T a commutative L-algebra of finite étale correspondences on 𝒳. Suppose maximal ideals m,m′ satisfy (⊕_{h>1,q≥0}H^q_cris(X^{(h)}/W)⊗_{Z_p}L)_m=(...)_{m′}=0. There exist t∈T∖m and t′∈T∖m′, chosen from the model and its correspondence action independently of the cycles, such that for every c∈Z^d(X)^0_L and c′∈Z^{d′}(X)^0_L with d+d′=n, (i) (supp 𝒞)_s∩(supp 𝒞′)_{s′}=∅ for EVERY s,s′∈T, and (ii) codim_{X^{(h)}}(supp 𝒞′∩X^{(h)})≥d′ for every h≥1, the three classes AJ(t*c), AJ(t′*c′), and e(t*c,t′*c′) lie respectively in H¹_f(K,H), H¹_f(K,H′), and H¹_f(K,E_{t′*c′}). Here 𝒞,𝒞′ are the closures of the supports, and 1≤d,d′≤n−1; zero inputs use the split conventions.
hypotheses: The disjointness hypothesis quantifies over the whole algebra T, not just the final t,t′.
The codimension condition is asymmetric and imposed on the second cycle on every special-fiber intersection.
L may be a finite product of p-adic fields, handled componentwise.
proofSteps: Let I annihilate all deeper strata and let J′ annihilate all complementary idempotent summands of H¹(K,H^{2r−1}(X_Kbar,L(r))) for 1≤r≤n−1 outside m′. The finite image of T gives J′∖m′≠∅.

Choose t′=t′₁t′₂ with t′₁∈J′∖m′ and t′₂∈I^{4n−5}∖m′. Apply supported-finite-abel-jacobi with the whole model to c′ after t′₁: the dual marginal extension is finite and belongs to the selected crystalline summand. Invoke finite-condition-pushout.
Choose t₁∈I^{4n−5}∖m and apply the same proper-case theorem to c; its first marginal is finite.

Use the integral open 𝒰=𝒳∖(supp 𝒞′)_{t′}. Its d-density follows from d+d′=n and the codimension assumption; saturated disjointness puts the first support in the required 𝒰_{t₂}. Choose t₂∈I^{4n−5}∖m. The third application gives the full extension finite over K_𝒰, with target H_c(U) before pushout, and t=t₁t₂.

Apply the pushout for K and K_𝒰: the only obstruction left is the valuation line H¹(K,L(1))/H¹_f(K,L(1)). Restriction multiplies valuations by the nonzero ramification index, hence is injective after tensoring L. The full class is therefore finite over K.

sources.match: The main theorem combines the supported finite-class theorem three times with a localized finite-condition pushout.

acceptance: The same t,t′ must work for every pair of cycles satisfying the two geometric conditions.
Reject a version needing disjointness only for the selected pair of correspondences.
Descent uses the valuation quotient of L(1), not a general descent assertion for potentially crystalline classes.

nodes.title: Disjoint closures on a smooth model
nodes.statement: If 𝒳/O_K is proper smooth, X_K projective, n<p, and geometrically trivial cycles of complementary codimensions d+d′=n have disjoint closures, their two Abel–Jacobi extensions and their full mixed extension are finite. For each field factor L_i of L, take T=L_i, m=m′=0 and t=t′=1, then assemble the conclusions over L. The zero ideal of a product with several field factors is not maximal. For global cycles satisfying HP.1’s (V1)–(V3), at a p-adic place with this smooth model their local canonical height lies in the completed unit subgroup.
hypotheses: For the height assertion retain the embedding in the prescribed V,V′ and all canonical-height hypotheses, including G1’s unresolved proof obligation.
Replacing smooth by strictly semistable without deeper-stratum annihilation is not asserted.
proofSteps: There are no h>1 strata on a smooth model; hence I=T and the localization condition is automatic.
A horizontal cycle closure in a smooth model over a DVR meets the special fiber in codimension at least its generic codimension, so the second geometric hypothesis is satisfied.
Apply the main theorem with the identity correspondence. For the last assertion apply the local finite-iff-unit criterion.

sources.locator: Remark A.9, p. 327; Remark A.15, p. 331
sources.match: Gives the good-reduction test and the exact local-height consequence, without extending it to all semistable models.

acceptance: For curves this gives the finite Poincaré biextension of disjoint degree-zero divisor closures when p>2.
Strictly semistable reduction alone does not pass this corollary.

requests.need: For bounded-below equivariant sheaf towers on a site with discrete finite-level G-action, justify the continuous equivariant derived-sections/geometric-sections spectral sequence after Rlim and rationalization when all R¹lim H^q have finite p-power exponent. Include the limit topology, equivariant acyclic resolutions, finite flat local-domain W scalar restriction, flat extension to finite products of Frac(W)-extensions, and the natural first edge on the geometric kernel. This is the site/period-coefficient extension of the existing Milnor and continuous-cochain interfaces, not only the discrete group-quotient Hochschild–Serre theorem.

Provide the enhanced localization and Mayer–Vietoris diagrams with cup, proper-support trace and coefficient maps for p-invertible finite towers and rational limits. Include compatible cones for two possibly singular pure-codimension supports, the Kummer sign of the boundary trace, and Galois-equivariant pullback/degree-trace splitting for a proper generically finite alteration of smooth generic opens. Existing EDC.3 smooth-pair Gysin alone must not be applied to singular cycle supports.

Supply raw cycle groups, finite flat pullback, proper pushforward and their base-change/composition formulas before passing to rational equivalence. The finite étale span monoid algebra and its integral support transport are owned in HP.0; existing MC.0 Chow-correspondence action supplies its compatibility on Chow groups, not a replacement for raw cycle supports.

Supply exact/faithful strict D_dR and D_cris on their admissible representation categories, G-stable subquotient functoriality, semistable finite-condition complexes and two exact consequences: (a) a semistable monodromy-pure weight −1 V has H¹_st=H¹_f, by the absence of φ=p⁻¹ on D_st(V)/ND_st(V); (b) for a crystalline pure weight −1 summand W of H∨(1) and a finite dual extension class supported in W, 0→H¹_f(L(1))→H¹_f(E)→H¹_f(H)→0 for all finite base extensions, with the complement split. Also retain the Tate-curve exceptional H⁰(V⁻) terms in the canonical local mixed-extension calculation. This is an extension of the listed period/weak-admissibility nodes, not an assumption that all crystalline extensions stay crystalline.

Extend the proper potential-semistability interface to H^q_et(Y_Kbar,Q_p) of smooth separated algebraic Y/K, with localization, finite-extension descent data and G-stable subquotients, so the Abel–Jacobi extension realized in open-complement cohomology is potentially semistable. The existing proper-rigid theorem does not supply this smooth-open statement. A direct Nekovář 2000 Theorem 3.1 route can replace it once the primary proof is accessible.

Export the arithmetic good-prime consequence of the existing smooth proper finite-field purity theorem: combine good-reduction base change and its Galois equivariance to exclude Frobenius eigenvalue 1 on every G_K quotient of H^{2d−1}(X_Kbar,L(d)) at a good finite prime away from p. The finite-field purity theorem is already imported by its exact node ID. This request is its good-prime/base-change application, not a new purity theorem or a claim about quotients of arbitrary monodromy-pure local p-adic representations.

Add the integral site-level Kato/Sato interfaces for 0≤d<p−1: S(d)≃τ≤d i*Rj*μ_{p•}^{⊗d}; Sato T(d) and its logarithmic Hodge–Witt triangle; refined cycle classes with zero residue (Sato 2013 Proposition 9.10); support, cup and trace compatibility. Supply the finite-coefficient crystalline injectivity/base-change used in DL24 B.8 (Sato A.3.1/9.5), compatible Galois log-PD embedding systems and their divided-Frobenius complexes, p^a-almost comparison/finiteness giving B.21’s exact admissibility claims, the π_r equivalence for n−1≤r<p−1 on strict-pair boundary diagrams, and cup with the point Tate class for weight raising. Existing rational HK syntomic fibers and proper C_st comparison are imported; they do not by themselves supply these integral supported maps.

Use the existing principal-idele reciprocity and local compatibility to identify the p-completed finite-idelic quotient Γ_{K,p}, its finite generation as a Z_p-module, and the local completed K_v× maps into it; prove the almost-everywhere vanishing and principal-relation exactness used when summing the local height indices. The underlying Artin maps and idele carriers remain upstream-owned.

Refine RD.4/supported-log-weight-spectral-sequence in its proper strictly semistable case to the Frobenius/monodromy-compatible Mokrane weight sequence used in DL24 proof of A.8, pp. 346–347. Specify the E₁ stratum summands with their Tate twists, restriction/Gysin differentials, correspondence action and convergence to Hyodo–Kato cohomology; retain Nφ=pφN and the filtration shift of N. Prove that if every h>1 stratum group vanishes after localization, only the untwisted h=1 term in column zero survives, the induced N is zero, and degree q has the smooth proper Frobenius weight q. RD.4 currently specifies only underlying K₀-vector spaces and explicitly leaves Frobenius twists unspecified; that interface alone cannot prove HP.4’s crystalline pure summand. Use the existing CR.6 complex and PH proper comparison, without adding another weight-sequence owner.

gaps.title: Canonical local Hodge splitting with exceptional quotients
gaps.detail: The defining local torsor splitting and finite-iff-unit criterion are stated in DL24 A.7/A.15, but the full proof cited to Nekovář 1993 §§1–4 and 7 was not accessible. SC §11.3 constructs a norm height and §11.4 corrects it under additional valuation and logarithmic invertibility hypotheses; it does not justify identifying that restricted construction with the general A.7 canonical local height. Verify the original filtered-semistable mixed-extension construction, its exceptional H⁰(V⁻) terms and normalization before claiming closure. This gap affects the canonical height proof, not the separate B.9/B.11/A.8 chain.
